scenes.title: Provisioning Cloud Resources
scenes.narration: You can create cloud resources by clicking in the console, scripting with the CLI, or declaring them as code with tools like Terraform for repeatable infrastructure.

scenes.title: Three Ways to Provision
bullets: The console is great for exploring and learning but is manual and hard to reproduce.
The CLI lets you script actions, which is repeatable but still imperative.
Infrastructure as Code declares the desired state, giving version-controlled, reviewable infra.
scenes.narration: There are three common ways to build cloud infrastructure. The console is visual and perfect for learning, though every click is manual and easy to forget. The CLI adds scripting and repeatability while remaining step-by-step. Infrastructure as Code goes further by declaring the end state you want, so infrastructure becomes version-controlled and reviewable.

scenes.title: Imperative vs. Declarative
scenes.narration: An imperative approach like the CLI runs a sequence of commands and leaves you to track what exists. A declarative tool instead lets you describe the desired end state and figures out the changes needed to reach it. For infrastructure meant to last, the declarative model is far safer and more maintainable.

scenes.title: Declaring a Bucket in Terraform
scenes.narration: This Terraform configuration, shown in its JSON form, declares an S3 bucket as code. Instead of clicking through the console, you describe the bucket and its tags, then let Terraform create or update it to match. Because this definition lives in version control, every change is reviewed, repeatable, and easy to roll back.

scenes.text: Explore with the console, script with the CLI, but manage lasting infrastructure as code — declarative, version-controlled infra is the professional standard.
scenes.narration: Use the console to learn and the CLI for quick tasks, but treat production infrastructure as code. Declarative, version-controlled definitions are the standard for building cloud systems that stay consistent and auditable.
